los_dc_median.label: Median ED time, discharged patients
los_dc_median.source: CMS Care Compare OP-18b: CMS Care Compare 'Timely and Effective Care - Hospital' (Provider Data Catalog yv7e-xc69, release 2026-08-13), Facility ID (CCN) 310038 ROBERT WOOD JOHNSON UNIVERSITY HOSPITAL, ONE ROBERT WOOD JOHNSON PLACE, NEW BRUNSWICK NJ; measure OP_18b score, sample 408 s
los_dc_median.note: CMS computes the median from a sample of 408 visits; interval = +/- 1.96 standard errors of a sample median of a lognormal stay with cv 0.9 (30 min). Excludes admitted, transferred and psychiatric patients; the simulator's discharged patients are compared.

lwbs_rate.label: Left without being seen, share of arrivals
lwbs_rate.source: CMS Care Compare OP-22: CMS Care Compare 'Timely and Effective Care - Hospital' (Provider Data Catalog yv7e-xc69, release 2026-08-13), Facility ID (CCN) 310038 ROBERT WOOD JOHNSON UNIVERSITY HOSPITAL, ONE ROBERT WOOD JOHNSON PLACE, NEW BRUNSWICK NJ; measure OP_22 score 1 percent, den
lwbs_rate.note: Published as a whole-number percent, so the true value is anywhere in the interval. The fit is indifferent inside +/- 0.3 points of the published value and penalises anything further out.

arrivals_per_day.label: ED arrivals per day
arrivals_per_day.source: ed_visits_per_year_cms: CMS Care Compare 'Timely and Effective Care - Hospital' (Provider Data Catalog yv7e-xc69, release 2026-08-13), Facility ID (CCN) 310038 ROBERT WOOD JOHNSON UNIVERSITY HOSPITAL, ONE ROBERT WOOD JOHNSON PLACE, NEW BRUNSWICK NJ; denominator ('Sample') of measure
arrivals_per_day.note: The arrival rate is a simulator input (patient.shared.arrivals_per_day), so this only checks the arrival process (hour/weekday/season profile over the simulated window).

ward_occupancy.label: Inpatient occupancy (modelled ward pool)
ward_occupancy.source: inpatient_occupancy: CMS HCRIS hospital cost report (form CMS-2552-10), FY2024 file, report 811005 for CCN 310038, fiscal year 01/01/2024-12/31/2024; Worksheet S-3 Part I line 14: inpatient days 211651 / bed days available 228750
ward_occupancy.note: Public figures: HCRIS cost report, annual, beds available: 0.925; HHS weekly capacity reports, staffed beds: 0.850, weekly range 0.70-0.96. Both are averages over ALL inpatient beds of the hospital; the simulator has one pool of beds that ED admissions compete for, and matching that pool's occupancy to the hospital-wide figure is an assumption. The fit aims at 0.925 (HCRIS cost report, annual, beds available); the acceptance interval spans the usable public figures +/- 3 points. CAPPED: the fit aims at 0.891, not 0.925. A single pool of 168 beds run at 0.925 leaves fewer free beds than 1.5 standard deviations of its own demand; in the simulator that is not a steady state (a 1-2 % seasonal rise in arrivals plus the literature boarding penalty make it fill for weeks, and LWBS doubles on held-out seeds - found in the first calibration run of RWJUH). The published figure is an average over a hospital several times larger, where the same occupancy leaves far more slack in absolute beds.

ward_occupancy_drift.label: Ward occupancy drift (last 10 days minus first 10)
ward_occupancy_drift.source: model requirement, not a published figure
ward_occupancy_drift.note: A baseline must be a steady state: a hospital's published annual figures cannot come from a pool that is still filling. Near-full pools drift because boarding lengthens stays (literature penalty), which feeds back into occupancy.

ed_salaries_per_day.label: ED salaries per day (wages, no benefits, no physicians)
ed_salaries_per_day.source: ed_salaries_per_year: CMS HCRIS hospital cost report (form CMS-2552-10), FY2024 file, report 811005 for CCN 310038, fiscal year 01/01/2024-12/31/2024 (report status code 1); Worksheet A line 91 'EMERGENCY', column 1 (salaries)
ed_salaries_per_day.note: Published: 74.8 k$/day (HCRIS Worksheet A line 91 column 1 = salaries the hospital pays in the Emergency cost centre, / 365). Compared with the simulator's wage bill WITHOUT benefits and WITHOUT attending / resident pay. Three things the report does not say widen the interval: it counts paid hours, the simulator worked hours (paid/worked 1.0 to 1.15 allowed); employed attending physicians may or may not be on the line (up to 12 % of the bill allowed); +/- 10 % for wage levels (the simulator uses BLS area wages). The fit aims at the middle of the interval. In the model this target mostly decides how many nurses are on the floor, which patient flow alone cannot identify.

search.description: 3 rounds x 256 candidates x 10 seeds, 37 simulated days each after a 7-day warm-up: 159 of 768 candidates (21 %) were inside every hospital-specific interval (round 1, drawn half from the whole box and half around the point calibration: 14 of 256). 41 spread-out candidates were re-simulated on 32 held-out seeds for 45 days; 1 no longer passed and were dropped; 24 members kept (including member 0).
